blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Tamil Nadu's economy is highly diversified, spanning agriculture, advanced manufacturing, and service industries.
Major industrial pillars include Automobile manufacturing, Textiles, Leather production, and IT/Electronics.
Industrial Corridors and Special Economic Zones (SEZs) foster targeted economic development across the state.
The state's commercial capability is fortified by major sea ports and a well-developed power sector.

blocks.content: Tamil Nadu has one of the strongest state economies in India. It consistently ranks among the top three states by GDP. The state has a diversified economy with strong presence in manufacturing, services, and agriculture.

items: GDP (GSDP): Among top 3 states in India (approximately Rs. 25 lakh crore in 2023-24)
Per capita income: Among the highest in India
Manufacturing contributes over 25% of GSDP
Export-oriented economy: Chennai is called 'Detroit of India' for auto manufacturing

blocks.content: Agriculture employs about 20% of Tamil Nadu's workforce. Tamil Nadu is a leading producer of several crops. The Kaveri delta (Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Nagapattinam) is the main rice-growing area, known as the 'Granary of South India.'

The Chennai-Hosur corridor is a major automotive hub. Chennai accounts for nearly 35% of India's automobile production and 40% of auto component exports. Major companies: Hyundai (Sriperumbudur), Ford (Maraimalai Nagar, now closed), BMW assembly (Chennai), Daimler (Oragadam), Renault-Nissan (Oragadam), Royal Enfield (Oragadam and Tiruvottiyur), TVS Motor Company (Hosur).

Tamil Nadu is India's largest textile producer. Coimbatore ('Manchester of South India'), Tiruppur ('Knit Capital of India'), and Erode are major textile hubs. Kancheepuram (Kanjivaram silk), Bhavani (Bhavani Jamakkalam carpet), and Madurai (cotton dhotis) are known for traditional textiles.

rows: Vehicle assembly, heavy transport manufacturing, and automotive components
Yarn production, powerlooms, handlooms, and ready-made garment exports
Software services, technology parks, and electronic hardware manufacturing
Tanning processing, footwear manufacturing, and finished leather exports

blocks.content: Chennai is the second largest IT hub in India after Bengaluru. Major IT companies including TCS, Infosys, Wipro, Cognizant, Accenture, and Capgemini have large operations in Chennai. TIDEL Park in Taramani was one of India's first IT parks.
Tamil Nadu produces about 60% of India's leather. Vellore, Ranipet, and Chennai are the major centres. Ambur (Vellore district) is famous for leather footwear.

items: Neyveli Lignite Corporation (NLC): Thermal power from lignite; Cuddalore district
North Chennai Thermal Power Plant: Major thermal plant; Chennai
Mettur Thermal Power Plant: Salem district
Nuclear Power: Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant (Tirunelveli) – Russia-aided; largest nuclear power plant in India
Wind Energy: Tamil Nadu is India's leading state in wind energy; Muppandal Wind Farm (Tirunelveli) is Asia's largest wind farm
Solar Energy: TN has large solar parks in Ramanathapuram and Thoothukudi
